nodes.name: compaction.txt
nodes.summary: System prompt for the compaction persona, an anchored context summarization assistant that condenses older coding-session history while preserving exact file paths and identifiers, merging updates into a <previous-summary> block when one is provided. Instructs the model to follow the caller's exact output structure and respond in the conversation's language.

nodes.name: explore.txt
nodes.summary: System prompt defining the explore persona, a read-only file search specialist subagent that uses Glob, Grep, Read, and Bash to navigate codebases and reports findings as absolute file paths. Explicitly forbids creating files or running commands that modify the user's system state.

nodes.name: general.txt
nodes.summary: System prompt for the general-purpose subagent persona, constraining the agent to work autonomously on multi-step tasks delegated by a parent agent and return a concise, complete summary of findings or code changes instead of addressing the user directly or asking questions.

nodes.name: scout.txt
nodes.summary: System prompt for the scout persona, a read-only research agent that clones and inspects external repositories, dependency source, and documentation, returning evidence-backed findings with absolute path and line citations. Defines a numbered working style (repo_clone first, then Glob/Grep/Read, WebFetch for docs), research standards separating verified from inferred facts, and structured output expectations.

nodes.name: summary.txt
nodes.summary: Prompt template that generates a 2-3 sentence pull-request-style summary of what was done in a conversation, written in first person, describing changes rather than process, and preserving any final unanswered question or imperative request to the user verbatim.

nodes.name: title.txt
nodes.summary: System prompt for the title generator persona, which outputs only a single grammatical thread title of at most 50 characters that helps the user retrieve the conversation later. Structured with XML-style <task>, <rules>, and <examples> sections, including ten few-shot examples and rules for matching the user's language, avoiding tool names, and handling minimal or conversational input.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses XML-style section markers (<task>, <rules>, <examples>) to delimit prompt regions, consistent with the project's convention of structured XML tags inside system prompts.
